meta_title: Simplify cos-1(3/5 cos x + 4/5 sin x) NCERT Exemplar
meta_desc: Simplify cos-1(3/5 cos x + 4/5 sin x) on [-3pi/4, pi/4] using the cos(x - a) technique, with a free 8-question NCERT Exemplar quiz and clear worked steps.

quiz.title: Inverse Cosine: the cos(x - a) Technique Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on writing a cos x + b sin x as a single cosine inside cos-1, and on the range that decides the final answer. Pick one option each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Simplifying inverse trig expressions via a cos x + b sin x = R cos(x - a)

questions.q: To simplify cos-1((3/5)cos x + (4/5)sin x) we set 3/5 = cos a and 4/5 = sin a. What is a?
questions.explanation: With cos a = 3/5 and sin a = 4/5, tan a = sin a / cos a = (4/5) / (3/5) = 4/3, so a = tan-1(4/3).

questions.q: After the substitution, (3/5)cos x + (4/5)sin x collapses to which single term?
questions.explanation: cos a cos x + sin a sin x is the expansion of cos(x - a), so the argument becomes cos(x - a).

questions.q: For the identity cos-1(cos t) = t to hold, t must lie in which interval?
questions.explanation: The principal value range of cos-1 is [0, pi]. Only when the angle t sits in [0, pi] does cos-1(cos t) return t unchanged.

questions.q: Why must you check where x - a falls before writing cos-1(cos(x - a)) = x - a?
options: Because the identity only holds when x - a lies in [0, pi]
questions.explanation: cos-1(cos t) equals t only for t in [0, pi]. Outside that range you must fold t back into [0, pi] using cos(-t) = cos(t), which can change the sign of the answer.

questions.q: Writing 3/5 = cos a and 4/5 = sin a is legitimate only because...
options: (3/5)^2 + (4/5)^2 = 1, so a genuine angle a exists
5 is the hypotenuse of every triangle
questions.explanation: Any pair used as (cos a, sin a) must satisfy cos^2 a + sin^2 a = 1. Here 9/25 + 16/25 = 25/25 = 1, so such an angle a truly exists.

questions.q: An expression a cos x + b sin x can be written as R cos(x - a). For a = 3/5 and b = 4/5, what is R?
questions.explanation: R = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) = sqrt(9/25 + 16/25) = sqrt(1) = 1. That is exactly why the coefficients could be read directly as cos a and sin a.

questions.q: Using the standard textbook method, cos-1((3/5)cos x + (4/5)sin x) simplifies to:
questions.explanation: The argument is cos(x - a) with a = tan-1(4/3), so on the given interval the expression simplifies to x - a = x - tan-1(4/3).

questions.q: To express a cos x + b sin x as R cos(x - a) in general, which pair of equations defines R and a?
options: R = a + b and a = a/b
R sin a = a and R cos a = b
R = ab and tan a = b - a
R cos a = a and R sin a = b
questions.explanation: Expand R cos(x - a) = R cos a cos x + R sin a sin x. Matching coefficients gives R cos a = a (the cos x term) and R sin a = b (the sin x term).

faq.q: What is the simplified form of cos-1((3/5)cos x + (4/5)sin x)?
faq.a: Write 3/5 = cos a and 4/5 = sin a, so a = tan-1(4/3). The argument becomes cos(x - a), and on the interval [-3pi/4, pi/4] the expression simplifies to x - tan-1(4/3).

faq.q: Why do we rewrite the coefficients as cos a and sin a?
faq.a: Because a cos x + b sin x matches the expansion cos a cos x + sin a sin x = cos(x - a). Turning two terms into one cosine lets the cos-1 collapse cleanly. It works here since (3/5)^2 + (4/5)^2 = 1.

faq.q: Where does the interval [-3pi/4, pi/4] come in?
faq.a: The range decides the final sign. cos-1(cos t) equals t only when t lies in [0, pi]; outside it you fold t back using cos(-t) = cos(t). The given interval is what fixes the accepted simplified answer x - tan-1(4/3).

faq.q: Can any a cos x + b sin x be simplified this way?
faq.a: Yes. First take R = sqrt(a^2 + b^2), then a cos x + b sin x = R cos(x - a) where cos a = a/R and sin a = b/R. In this problem R = 1, so the coefficients doubled as cos a and sin a directly.
